title: Krishna's Mission
body:
Krishna's Mission

Despite the massive military preparations on both sides, Sree Krishna resolved to make one final, solemn attempt to avert a catastrophic war that would annihilate the kshatriya race. He travelled to Hastinapura as an emissary of peace. Recognising the gravity of his visit, the citizens of Hastinapura thronged the streets to catch a glimpse of the Lord, while Duryodhana prepared lavish presents, chariots, and a grand feast in an attempt to buy Krishna's favour.
Sree Krishna bypassed Duryodhana's palace and chose to stay at Vidura's humble dwelling, spending the night in quiet conversation and comforting Kunti, who wept over the impending tragedy. The next morning, Krishna entered the royal court of Hastinapura. He declined Duryodhana's invitation to a feast, famously stating that an emissary eats only after his mission is fulfilled. Addressing King Dhritarashtra, Krishna made a powerful and moving plea for peace, asking for only five villages for the five Pandava brothers to settle the dispute honourably.
Dhritarashtra expressed his agreement but confessed his absolute powerlessness over his sons. Sree Krishna then turned to Duryodhana, urging him to abandon his envy and save his race from destruction. Bhishma, Drona, and Vidura joined in pressing Duryodhana to accept Krishna's advice. Furious at being publicly admonished, Duryodhana declared that the Pandavas had forfeited their kingdom at play, and that he would never yield to threats, refusing to return even a single needle-point of territory.
Duryodhana and his associates plotted to seize Sree Krishna and bind him. Sensing their devious plan, Krishna laughed and revealed his cosmic Visvarupa form in the open assembly. The blind Dhritarashtra, by the Lord's grace, temporarily regained his sight to behold the magnificent vision of Sree Krishna permeating the entire universe. Having witnessed the Lord's supreme divinity, Dhritarashtra begged to be made blind again, refusing to look upon any worldly object thereafter. Sree Krishna departed from the court, his peace mission failed, making the Great War an absolute certainty.

सर्वधर्मान् परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ।।

Translation: "Abandon all varieties of dharmas and simply surrender unto Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sinful reactions; do not fear." — Verse Gita XVIII-66
